thread:
Marcus (support): Hey team — incoming escalation from AcmeMaps: iOS app is getting cut off mid-stream when users swap from cellular -> cafe WiFi. Customer says the last partial JSON chunk is returned and the connection just closes. Billing shows tokens consumed for the aborted request. 😕

Anya (AcmeMaps): Yup — happening on ~10% of sessions. Steps: start a long generation (~>600 tokens), flip from 5G -> public WiFi, sometimes we get: a final partial line like `data: {\"choices\": [{\"delta\": \"...text\"` then socket closes. No 4xx/5xx in the app, just an EOF on the SSE stream. We can reproduce on iOS 16 and a Samsung S22 with Android 13.

Marcus (support): Thanks. Can you paste a minimal reproduce curl+headers and the exact server response bytes (hex or raw) if you have them? Also which model/endpoint and region?

Anya (AcmeMaps): Repro curl we used:

```\ncurl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \\\\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\\\n  \"https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=gen-4-large&region=us-west\"\n```

App saw: first ~580 tokens then a last line that looked truncated, app event handler got connection close. We attached a Wireshark capture (link) but summary: TLS session ends with TCP RST from client side when net switches, or we see FIN from mobile network.

Lia (eng): Thanks — two things we need to check: 1) whether the edge LB is logging a proxied response close (so we know if the server finished the response), and 2) whether partial chunks were flushed from runtime to the edge. Marcus, can you ask for the customer request-id header (x-rwd-request-id) or the exact timestamp?

Anya (AcmeMaps): We don't have rwd-id in app logs because we obfuscate headers, but the app logs show start ts 2026-03-15T14:22:09Z and close at 14:22:21Z. Token used was a short-lived key we create (TTL 60m).

Jordan (sre): I pulled edge logs for that minute window in us-west. I see the connection from the runtime to edge returned multiple SSE chunks and then the edge recorded a `client_closed` at 14:22:21. No 5xx from the edge. Server indicates generation completed and streamed final bytes at 14:22:21. So it looks like the client/network aborted, not a server crash.

Marcus (support): Customer reports billing charged for the whole request though — can we explain why tokens billed if client closed?

Lia (eng): Billing is based on tokens emitted by the model runtime. If runtime finished generating and handed tokens to the output stream, tokens are counted even if the client disconnects before receiving every byte. If generation completed before the TCP FIN, those tokens are billable. If the runtime was interrupted mid-generation, we should have a partial token accounting still. We can correlate the runtime logs (generation_end vs connection_close) with billing events.

Anya (AcmeMaps): Ok that's fair, but customer wants a way to avoid paying for full runs when their mobile flips. Any mitigation?

Lia (eng): Short term: implement client-side heuristics — detect rapid network-change events and cancel the request gracefully (send a cancel to the server if possible) so runtime knows to abort. For iOS specifically, increase the keepalive interval and use `Connection: keep-alive` and send periodic small pings to the endpoint to reduce sockets being torn down by NAT. Also, on our side we can add a flag to allow server to stop generation on socket close earlier (best-effort) — I'll open a small follow-up ticket.

Jordan (sre): Also check if the mobile OS is issuing a hard RST on handoff (some carriers do) — that will look like immediate socket reset and prevents graceful shutdown. For those cases, client cannot avoid token usage if runtime completes in that window.

Marcus (support): For reproduction, can you try a curl that simulates a late FIN? Example: start the curl, then `kill -9` the curl process to mimic abrupt client RST. We've observed similar behavior.

Anya (AcmeMaps): We tried killing the app process and saw same billing behavior.

Lia (eng): Logging/data requests for eng: please collect the following and attach here:
- raw edge request id (x-rwd-request-id) if possible
- TLS session id + SNI (to see if any intermediate proxy)
- exact first/last runtime log lines around generation (we want generation_start, token_flush events, generation_end)
- client side socket close (app logs)

Marcus (support): I'll ask the customer for those. Meanwhile, quick mitigation suggestions for them: reduce max tokens per request (so partial runs bill less), enable incremental commit on your app (store partial output on disk to surface to users), and implement exponential reconnect for SSE rather than immediate restart. :thumbsup:

Anya (AcmeMaps): Got it. We'll collect the logs. One last ask: can you confirm whether token billing rounds up to the last emitted token or if we ever charge for tokens that weren't streamed because the client dropped before flush?

Lia (eng): We charge for tokens that the runtime emitted to the output stream. If the runtime emitted but the edge didn't flush to the client before client aborted, tokens are still emitted and billable. If runtime aborted mid-token and didn't emit, that should not be billed. We'll run a quick audit for the customer's request window once we have the request-id.

deploy-bot: Deployed patch rwd/streaming:soft-abort-v1 to canary (us-west) at 2026-03-16T02:10:00Z — adds earlier runtime check on socket EOF to avoid continuing extra generation after client close (best-effort; may still bill emitted tokens).

Lia (eng): Note: that canary will attempt to stop generation on detection of socket EOF, but it's best-effort due to buffering and kernel-level TCP semantics. We'll monitor for regressions.

Marcus (support): Thanks all — Anya we'll follow up once we get the rwd-request-id and the captures. For now share the app logs and whether the clients show OS-level network handoff event just before close.

Anya (AcmeMaps): Will do, thx everyone.
